text: Domnu is an obscure Irish goddess. She is also called Déa Dumnu. The Book of Invasions names her as the ancestral mother of the Fomorians. The magical Tuatha Dé Danann defeated the Fomorians. Scholars read the Tuatha Dé as gods of the arriving Celts. They read the Fomorians as an earlier people. So Domnu may be an ancestral goddess of early Celtic or pre-Celtic Ireland. Her name translates as deep. This suggests she rules the ocean depths or the misty depths of the Otherworld. Inver Domnann, or Broadhaven, in County Sligo may take its name from her.
objective: Record Domnu as the obscure Irish mother-goddess of the Fomorians.
